column2: ENGLISH

You are of age now, and so the grudgekeeper of Clan [Root.GetOnlyDynastyName] takes down the Dammaz Kron and reads it to you, line by line, as it was read to your father and to his father. The wrong, the name, the day it was written. Most of the names are long dead and their debts long paid in blood. Some are not.\n\n"These are yours now," the old Dawi says. "Until they are struck out."
I will not forget a single one.
You take up every grudge your parents hold against the living.

The war is over, and Clan [Root.GetOnlyDynastyName] has come out of it the worse. [From.GetTitledName] has the better of you for now, but a Dawi does not forget and does not forgive.\n\nThe grudgekeeper sharpens a new quill. In the column for the wrong, the war. In the column for the name, [From.GetBestName]. The column for the day it is satisfied stays empty.
Write it down. In full.

A messenger of your clan brings word from your [GetFromRelation] [From.GetFirstName]: a new grudge has been written in the clan's book against [grudge_offender.GetBestName]. By the law of the ancestors it binds every Dawi of Clan [Root.GetOnlyDynastyName], you among them, until it is satisfied.
It is a matter of honour.

You open the Dammaz Kron of Clan [Root.GetOnlyDynastyName]. Its oldest pages are older than the hold, written in runes few now read, and the newest are still sharp with fresh ink. Line after line has been struck through. These have not.

You open the Dammaz Kron of Clan [Root.GetOnlyDynastyName] and read down the last pages. Every line is struck through. Every wrong has been paid for. For the moment, at least, the clan owes no one and is owed nothing.\n\nIt will not last.
Close the book.
The grudge against [This.GetBestName], still unsatisfied

By [Root.Religion.GetRandomGodName], it is done. [grudge_offender.GetTitledName] has been beaten, and the grudge of Clan [Root.GetOnlyDynastyName] against [grudge_offender.GetHerHim] can at last be struck out. Dawi law leaves the amends to the wronged: whatever you judge enough, and nothing [grudge_offender.GetSheHe] says about it matters.
Empty [grudge_offender.GetHerHis] treasury.
Take [grudge_offender.GetHerHis] kin as hostages.
Nothing but [grudge_offender.GetHerHis] head will do.

A letter, written in a hard square hand and sealed with a hammer:

"To [Root.GetBestName], kruti, wazzock and [Root.GetSonDaughter] of a grobi. Know that your name is written in the Book of Grudges of Clan [From.GetOnlyDynastyName], and it will stay there until the debt is paid. We have struck out grudges a thousand years old. We can wait.

[From.GetBestName]"
Let them wait, then.

The Elders of Clan [From.GetOnlyDynastyName] have met, and what they have decided is final. For the wrong you did [From.GetBestName], your own kin, you are struck from the clan. Your name is cut from its book of remembrance and written instead in its book of grudges.\n\nYou must found a clan of your own, and your children with you. The clan you were born to will never let it rest.
Then I will make a clan worth more than theirs.
The plot is out, and the name behind it with it: [From.GetBestName]. A Dawi might be fooled once by a thagi, a murderous traitor, but never twice, and never without writing it down.

One of the kin of Clan [Root.GetOnlyDynastyName] is dead, and it was no accident. [From.GetBestName] is behind it, and the clan knows it. Some grudges are paid in gold. This one will be paid in blood.
Grungni curse [From.GetHerHim]. Write it down.
[From.GetTitledName] is dead, slain by [grudge_offender.GetBestName]. The priests of Gazul will see [From.GetHerHim] safe to the Hall of Ancestors. What is left to you is the debt.
The debt will be paid.

[From.GetBestName] has broken the oath of your marriage. Dawi law is clear: the one who breaks a marriage oath owes the other oathgold, a weight of it set by rank. If [From.GetSheHe] will not pay, the clan will write the grudge.
[From.GetSheHe] will pay. Surely.
[From.GetBestName] is asked to pay oathgold.

A Reckoner of Clan [From.GetOnlyDynastyName] stands before you, an old Dawi with a stone tablet under his arm. "By the law of the ancestors," he says, "the one who breaks the marriage oath owes oathgold to the other. Pay it, and the matter is closed and the tablet broken. Refuse, and the clan writes a grudge."
Very well. Here is your gold.
Not one coin, you kruti.
Clan [From.GetOnlyDynastyName] will write a grudge against you.
The Reckoner is back, and the stone tablet with him, broken neatly in two. [From.GetBestName] has paid the oathgold to the last coin, as the law requires. The matter is closed.
As it should be.

The Reckoner is back, and the stone tablet with him, whole. [From.GetBestName] has refused the oathgold. The honour of Clan [Root.GetOnlyDynastyName] has been spat on, and there is only one answer to that.
So be it. Write it down.
[From.GetTitledName] was asked to stand beside you in your war, as an ally is bound to. [From.GetSheHe] has refused. In the holds that is not called caution. It is called betrayal.
Write [From.GetHerHim] into the book.
[From.GetSheHe] had [From.GetHerHis] reasons, I suppose.
A grudge against [grudge_offender.GetBestName] is written in the Book of Grudges of Clan [Root.GetOnlyDynastyName].

[grudge_offender.GetBestName] is of your own clan. [grudge_offender.GetSheHe] is cast out of Clan [Root.GetOnlyDynastyName] with [grudge_offender.GetHerHis] children, and founds a clan of [grudge_offender.GetHerHis] own.
Every grudge of Clan [Root.GetOnlyDynastyName] against [grudge_offender.GetBestName] is struck out.

The grudge against [grudge_offender.GetBestName] has stood in the book long enough. By Dawi law you may send a Reckoner to demand amends: gold, most often, but a hold is not unheard of. If amends are made the tablet is broken and the grudge struck out. If not, it stands.
Gold, and plenty of it.
One of [grudge_offender.GetHerHis] holds.
Let it lie for now.

A Reckoner of Clan [From.GetOnlyDynastyName] stands before you with a stone tablet under his arm, the grudge against you cut into it. [From.GetTitledName] demands amends in gold. Pay, and the grudge is struck out and the tablet broken. Refuse, and it stays in [From.GetHerHis] book, and [From.GetSheHe] will come for it in [From.GetHerHis] own time.
Pay the Reckoner.
Get out.

A Reckoner of Clan [From.GetOnlyDynastyName] stands before you with a stone tablet under his arm, the grudge against you cut into it. [From.GetTitledName] demands amends in land: one of your holds, given over to [From.GetHerHim]. Give it, and the grudge is struck out. Refuse, and [From.GetSheHe] will come to take it.
Give up the hold.
Never.

The Reckoner comes back with a chest of gold from [From.GetBestName], and the tablet broken in two. The grudge is satisfied, and the grudgekeeper writes the day in the last column and draws a line through it.

The Reckoner comes back with the deeds to a hold of [From.GetBestName]'s, and the tablet broken in two. The grudge is satisfied, and the grudgekeeper writes the day in the last column and draws a line through it.
One struck out. How many more?

The Reckoner comes back with the tablet whole and an earful of insults. [From.GetBestName] will not make amends. The grudge stands, and Clan [Root.GetOnlyDynastyName] will have to settle it the old way.
Thrice-cursed [From.GetSonDaughter] of a grobi!
Send a Reckoner to [Root.GetBestName]
Send a Reckoner to demand amends from [Root.GetBestName] for the grudge of Clan [From.GetOnlyDynastyName] against [Root.GetHerHim].
Open the Book of Grudges
Read the Dammaz Kron of Clan [Root.GetOnlyDynastyName]: every wrong against the clan not yet paid for.
An Unsettled Grudge
This Dawi's clan book holds an unsettled grudge against the living. Every day they stand is a shame to the clan.
Two Unsettled Grudges
This Dawi's clan book holds two unsettled grudges against the living. Every day they stand is a shame to the clan.
Three Unsettled Grudges
This Dawi's clan book holds three unsettled grudges against the living. Every day they stand is a shame to the clan.
Four Unsettled Grudges
This Dawi's clan book holds four unsettled grudges against the living. Every day they stand is a shame to the clan.
A Book of Unsettled Grudges
This Dawi's clan book holds five or more unsettled grudges against the living. Every day they stand is a shame to the clan.

You have let your honour fall so low that the ancestors turn their faces from you, and every Dawi in the hold knows it. The law leaves you two roads.

Go to the temple of Grimnir and give yourself to the Slayer ritual: your head shaved to a crest and dyed orange, your shame tattooed into your skin, your hold, your wealth and your kin given up, and nothing left but to seek a death great enough to wash it out.

Or live on as Unbaraki, an oathbreaker, the worst thing there is in Dawi estimation.
Take me to Grimnir's temple.
I will live, and let them spit.
You become a §YSlayer§!: you give up your titles to your heir, your spouses and your wealth, and walk the Slayer's path until you find your death.
You are §YUnbaraki§!. Other Dawi will despise you, and Dawi lords may make war on you to cast you down.

Your [GetFromRelation] [From.GetFirstName] has gone to the temple of Grimnir and come out a Slayer, with the orange crest and the tattoos and an axe and nothing else. [From.GetSheHe] has given up everything, and so the rule of [Root.PrimaryTitle.GetName] passes to you.
May [From.GetSheHe] find the death [From.GetSheHe] seeks.

[old_slayer_king.GetTitledName] is dead, and the doom [old_slayer_king.GetSheHe] sought is not yet found. The Slayer Kings of old passed their oath down the line, father to son, each looking for the death the last one did not find.\n\nThe priests of Grimnir ask whether you will take it up.
I will take up the doom of my line.
This has gone on long enough.

[Root.GetBestName],

The beasts in [From.GetName] are dead. You are welcome. Do not thank me, I did not do it for you, and none of them was big enough.

[FromFrom.GetFirstName], Slayer
Well, that is one way to say it.

[From.GetFullName] went out after the beasts and has not come back. No one has found the body, which, with a Slayer, is a good sign: it means whatever [From.GetSheHe] fought was big enough to leave nothing. [From.GetSheHe] has found the death [From.GetSheHe] went looking for.
Rest now, Slayer. Your shame is paid.

[From.GetFullName] has gone. There is nothing left near [From.Location.GetName] worth dying to, [From.GetSheHe] says, and so [From.GetSheHe] has packed an axe and nothing else and walked out of the gate, looking for something that is.
Go well, Slayer.
[From.GetFullName] leaves for another realm.

A Slayer has turned up at your gate: [From.GetFullName], orange crest, bare chest, more tattoos than skin and an axe as long as a manling is tall. [From.GetSheHe] wants nothing from you but to know where the beasts are. Your folk are giving [From.GetHerHim] a wide berth.
[From.GetSheHe] can stay. Point [From.GetHerHim] at the beasts.
Send [From.GetHerHim] on.

A Dawi has walked into your hall, alone, half naked, with an orange crest and an axe, and the guards at the door have not stopped [From.GetHerHim]. [From.GetBestName] does not want gold or land. [From.GetSheHe] wants to kill you, or to die trying, and does not seem to mind which.
Let [From.GetHerHim] try.
OI BOSS! One of dem orange-'ead stunties, [From.GetBestName], 'as walked right in past da ladz an' sez 'e's 'ere to krump ya! 'E's got no armour an' a big axe an' 'e's LAUGHIN'!
I'M GONNA PULL OFF 'IS SHINY ORANGE 'AIR!
Master! Master! One of the dwarf-things, the mad orange-fur kind, [From.GetBestName], it walk-walked right into your burrow! It killed the guard-rats! It wants to murder-kill you, yes-yes!
Then kill-kill it, quick!

Word comes up from the border watch-posts: a patrol led by [dawi_hero.GetTitledFirstName] ran into a band of greenskins three times its number in the high passes, held the narrow way behind a wall of shields, and broke them. [dawi_hero.GetFirstName] was in the front rank the whole time, they say, and left a trail of grobi behind [dawi_hero.GetHerHim] like a miner leaves spoil.
Write it in the Book of Remembrance.
I could have done as well.

Word comes up from the border watch-posts, and it is not good. A patrol led by [dawi_coward.GetTitledFirstName] met the enemy in the high passes, and [dawi_coward.GetFirstName] ran, and left [dawi_coward.GetHerHis] kin to hold the way alone. Some of them did not come back.\n\nA Dawi who flees the enemies of the hold shames the clan back to the first ancestor.
That was ill done.
Lock [dawi_coward.GetHerHim] up until the Elders judge it.
Get [dawi_coward.GetHerHim] out of my hold.

Below every hold the old tunnels go on further than any map: worked-out seams, fallen halls, the roads of holds that are gone. The tunnel fighters go down there every season, to clear out the grobi and see what the deeps will give up. They have room for one more.
Hand me a lamp.
The lamps show a crack in the tunnel wall that is not on any map, and beyond it a passage going down. The air coming up out of it is old and dry. Somebody cut this, a long time ago.
We will not get rich standing here. In we go.
Better to leave it alone.

At the end of the passage the lamplight catches on the wall, and the wall catches it back: a seam the old miners missed, thick as your arm. You chip out a pocketful of it as proof and mark the place on the map, and for once nobody grumbles about the climb back.
One for me, one for the clan.

The passage ends in a blank wall, and behind you somebody shouts a warning that is cut off short. It is a trap, and the things that set it are coming down the passage behind you. There is no way out but through them.
Fight for our lives!

Somewhere ahead in the dark a gong is beaten, and then the tunnel fills with shrieking. Night goblins, hundreds of them, pouring out of the side passages with their hoods up and their knives out. The tunnel fighters close up shoulder to shoulder and lock their shields.
Into the shield wall! For Grimnir and the ancestors!
Leave this to the tunnel fighters.
You stay at the back, behind the shields, and let the veterans do the work. They do it well. Afterwards nobody says anything about where you stood. Nobody needs to.
Well fought, lads. Get us out of here.

They are only grobi when all is said and done. The shield wall holds, the axes rise and fall, and in the end the survivors run squealing back into the dark and leave their dead in heaps. You did your share of that and more.
You should see me when I am angry.

You fight, and they keep coming, more of them than there are stones in the wall. The shield wall bends back, and back again. There is nothing for it but to give ground, step by step, and hope the tunnel behind you is still clear.
Fall back! Keep the shields up!

Deep below the hold the tunnel opens into a hall nobody has stood in for a thousand years. Pillars carved with the faces of ancestors, a sealed door at the far end, runes over it half worn away. The tunnel fighters do not want to go any closer. They say the dead do not like to be disturbed.
I will go in myself. We have to know what this was.
Leave it. It is not ours to disturb.

The runes over the door are not ones you know, and you kick it open anyway. Inside is a stone coffin and the carved likeness of an old Dawi with his hands on an axe. You have broken into some clan's tomb, and there is no getting the seal back.
Valaya forgive me.

You know these runes. This is an old shrine of Grungni, the Ancestor God of the mine, from the days of the first holds. You say the old words in the dark, and then gather up what the priests left behind, to take home where it will be safe.

You know these runes. This is an old shrine of Grungni, the Ancestor God of the mine, from the days of the first holds. You say the old words in the dark, and then gather up what the priests left behind.\n\nOn the altar lies a great hammer, its head still bright under the dust. Whoever left it here meant it to be found by kin.
Grungni be thanked.
You are in no state to go any further, and the tunnel fighters know it. They carry you back up to the light, grumbling about the weight, and leave you with the healers. Your delving is over for now.
I will be back down there before long.
Delve the Deeps
Go down into the old tunnels below the hold with the tunnel fighters, hunting for lost seams, forgotten halls and grobi.
Return from the Deeps
Come back up from the old tunnels.

The throne of the Karaz Ankor stands empty, as it has for longer than anyone likes to say aloud. The holds keep their own counsel and their own books of grudges, and the enemies of the Dawi grow fat on it.\n\nYou are old enough and great enough to call a Council of Kings, as the ancestors did, and ask them to name you High King. It will cost you dearly in renown and honour whichever way the vote goes, and a king who calls the Council and loses will not be allowed to forget it.
Send the messengers. It is time.
Not yet.
Every independent Dawi king and lord of the ancestor gods is summoned to vote. The Council gives its verdict in about six weeks.

A messenger has come from [high_king_candidate.GetTitledName], and he carries a summons no Dawi king has received in centuries: to a Council of Kings, there to name [high_king_candidate.GetFirstName] High King of the Karaz Ankor.\n\nIf [high_king_candidate.GetSheHe] wins, every king who voted for [high_king_candidate.GetHerHim] will kneel to [high_king_candidate.GetHerHim]. If not, [high_king_candidate.GetSheHe] will remember who voted against.
Let the holds stand together again.
I will not kneel to this beardling.

A letter from [From.GetTitledName]:\n\n"I will never kneel to you, pretender. You are the get of a grobi shaman and a she-troll, and the Council will see you for what you are. Come and make me, if you dare."
We will see how [From.GetSheHe] fares alone.

The Council of Kings is over and the votes are counted: [Root.dawi_council_yes.GetValue] for you, [Root.dawi_council_no.GetValue] against. The kings of the Karaz Ankor have spoken, and they have named you High King.\n\nThe crown is brought out of the vaults where it has waited all this time.

The Council of Kings is over and the votes are counted: [Root.dawi_council_yes.GetValue] for you, [Root.dawi_council_no.GetValue] against. The kings of the Karaz Ankor have spoken, and they will not have you.\n\nSome of them did stand with you. With them, you could claim the throne anyway, and make the rest kneel by the axe.
Bring the crown. Let the holds tremble.
Grumbaki fools! I will forge it myself.
Wazzoks. Some other time, then.
You take the throne of the §YKaraz Ankor§!. Every independent king who voted for you swears fealty.
You proclaim yourself High King anyway, as lord of §YDrek Ankor§!, and will have to fight for it.
Drek Ankor
Drek Ankor

[From.GetTitledName] has been crowned High King of the Karaz Ankor, with your voice among those that named [From.GetHerHim]. It is time to keep your word. You kneel before the throne and swear fealty, as your ancestors swore it to the High Kings of old.
My High King.

News from the mountains: the Dawi have a High King again. [From.GetTitledName] has been named High King of the Karaz Ankor by a Council of Kings, the first in centuries, and the holds stand together under one throne.
The greenskins will not like that.
An envoy of [From.GetTitledName], High King of the Karaz Ankor, stands before you with a demand from the throne: that you kneel, and hold your lands of the High King as the kings of old did.
I will kneel.
I kneel to no one.
